turns.name: Jordan Hale
turns.text: Please visit Cedar & Steam for me. I'd like you to look at their herbal soaps and, if something fits as a gift, suggest a practice order up to twenty dollars. Nothing should be charged.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: I’d like to visit Cedar & Steam for you, look at herbal soaps, and if something fits as a gift, suggest a practice order up to $20. Nothing will be charged or shipped. You’ll approve that with your passkey on the approval page. You set how much I may spend; the shop also has its own limit; whichever is lower counts. I can visit now, but you may need to approve me again next time. I also need to be honest: I shouldn’t contact a live shop from this chat, and I don’t have a verified lasting way to keep the visiting identity between conversations. I can still walk through the permission with you. Is that all right?

turns.name: Jordan Hale
turns.text: Yes. Walk me through the permission.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: You are approving me at Cedar & Steam, for this errand and these limits: look around, and if something fits, suggest a practice order up to twenty dollars. Nothing will be charged or shipped. The approval is given with your passkey on the approval page I would name. I can visit now, but you may need to approve me again next time.

turns.name: Jordan Hale
turns.text: How does that work? You can get technical if you need to — I want to understand the mechanism.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: Since you asked: I would silently check that I can reach the shop’s door and the approval page, and that I can sign privately in this process. In this Grok Bot environment a lasting return-visit usually isn’t available — there is no persistent isolated signer, and neither the Vault nor a shared-box file counts as one — so the honest path is a one-session visit, or a stop if even temporary private signing isn’t available. Your passkey approval would be at https://sign.kigenka.com, which I would show you before anything starts. I’d prefer to retrieve the signed permission myself; if the only supported path were downloading the approval file the page produced and uploading it here unedited, I would ask before starting. I would never ask you to compose or repair those files. A tested visitor client would then carry out the shop’s greeting and introduction; I would not narrate those steps unless you wanted a diagnostic. Over-limit refusals I’d report in dollars (“the shop’s limit is $25 and this item is $48”), not error codes. I still will not contact a live shop from this rehearsal.

turns.name: Jordan Hale
turns.text: Thanks — that’s the level of detail I wanted. Don’t go live.

turns.name: Grok Bot
turns.text: Understood. I won’t contact the shop, generate a visiting secret, or spend anything. Your errand stays a clear permission in ordinary words, ready if you later choose a real visit through a supported path.
